title: ambient failures in CNI with microk8s on Ubuntu 22.04 possibly due to ipv6 compatibility addresses
body:
### Is this the right place to submit this?

- [X] This is not a security vulnerability or a crashing bug
- [X] This is not a question about how to use Istio

### Bug Description

I wanted to test Ambient so I updated to 1.22.1 prior to trying and found that pods would get constantly disconnected and reconnected from the network and there was a furious amount of logging, the load on Loki made my system stress hard that it was logging so much.

After enabling Ambient on the namespace being tested the following type of messages were being logged.

Accepting that ipv6 support is in experimental stage I thought you should know anyway as it's possible the hard failure change between 1.22.0 and 1.22.1 might account for some of this.

It's been a few days since the last test - I just wanted to be sure I had looked at existing and previous issues plus changes for insight.

Running with stock Calico CNI otherwise - no changes apart from disabling some host internet connectivity (Ubuntu foo) that attempts to do this on all interfaces and produces spurious logged messages related to unreachable peers.

```
2024-06-09T15:12:59.358527Z  error  ambient  failed to add pod to ipset: test/redis-58db77c5b6-5dl2q failed to add IP :<nick>:10.1.43.8 with and proto 6 to ipset istio-inpod-probes: exist
2024-06-09T15:12:59.358529Z  error  ambient  failed to add pod to ztunnel: failed to add IP :<nick>:10.1.43.8 with and proto 6 to ipset istio-inpod-probes: exist
2024-06-09T15:12:59.358531Z  error  ambient  Failed to handle add event: failed to add IP :<nick>:10.1.43.8 with and proto 6 to ipset istio-inpod-probes: exist
2024-06-09T15:12:59.358625Z  error  cni  istio-cni cmdAdd failed to signal node Istio CNI agent: unable to push CNI event, error was 500
2024-06-09T15:12:59.358662Z  error  cni  istio-cni cmdAdd error: unable to push CNI event, error was 500
2024-06-09T15:12:59.358667Z  error  cni  istio-cni failed with: unable to push CNI event, error was 500
2024-06-09T15:12:59.377452Z  info  ambient  in pod mode - adding pod test/hop-b-7b79c8f74b-8jsfk to ztunnel
2024-06-09T15:12:59.377548Z  error  ambient  failed adding pod hop-b-7b79c8f74b-8jsfk to ipset istio-inpod-probes with ip :<nick>:10.1.43.45, error was failed to add IP :<nick>:10.1.43.45 with and proto 6 to ipset istio-inpod-probes: exist
```

For reference I have been running Istio for some time on this environment using sidecars with no problem and with CNI enabled using the overrides for the folder mentioned in the microk8s note ala..

```
    cni:
      cniBinDir: /var/snap/microk8s/current/opt/cni/bin
      cniConfDir: /var/snap/microk8s/current/args/cni-network
```

### Version

```Text
andrews@participant6 ~ % istioctl version
client version: 1.22.1
control plane version: 1.22.1
data plane version: 1.22.1 (10 proxies)
andrews@participant6 ~ % kubectl version
Client Version: v1.29.2
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.29.4
andrews@participant6 ~ %
```


### Additional Information

n/a at present as my mesh is back without Ambient but can post if necessary when experiencing the problem. I couldn't risk leaving this enabled due to the write load the logging was creating.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I'll probably re-test after disabling ipv6 soon and I'm assuming this specific problem will go away but this is a case that might appear again of course for other users. I'm assuming that the logs appear due to duplicate entries caused by attempting to set both <ipv4_addr> and :<nick>:<ipv4_addr> that could result in 'exist' from the configured rules.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Is this with `cni.ambient.ipv6=true` set or not?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 no, that option wasn't enabled in this config.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Ok, will try to reproduce myself but in the meantime you probably need that. I am working to make it on-by-default fwiw

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I am not entirely sure that will solve it though since this seems like ipv4-in-ipv6 addresses which might need some special consideration. But worth a shot if you have time

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Having added an /etc/sysctl.d/00-noipv6.conf to my nodes and restarted

```
net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1
net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1
net.ipv6.conf.lo.disable_ipv6=1
```

This specific issue, as anticipated, does not occur.

There are other issues but they are not directly related.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Interestingly after a few reboots the nodes ignored the sysctl config, not Istio related - some Ubuntu issue, but it caused the pods to start spinning logs again as above because of the ipv4-in-ipv6 mappings so I've had to disable ambient again on that namespace.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Oh interesting, I did not realize the ambient.ipv6 was added after 1.22 and not backported, sorry about the misdirection

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 no worries, I've got something I can work with to test now having also tweaked NetworkManager on my nodes to not rewrite the sysctls for IPv6 - everything seems stable for the time being to have a proper look at it.

@participant3 made the commit on 30th April but it looks like the 1.22.1 branch didn't pick that change but has more recent commits.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
What I can do, is bundle this all up into some sort of reproduction repository - I'm just using eksctl to spawn a pretty default flavoured cluster, adding istio via istioctl in ambient mode, adding cloudnative-pg and spawning a simple 3 replica cluster, and adding a cronjob that every minute spawns a pod to keep retry connecting to postgres until success.

Between these moving parts something goes quite wrong and causes the cluster networking to end up in a compromised state.

comments.author: participant2

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Is this something that can be solved by just disabling V6 entirely, and taking an updated ztunnel dev build that actually supports fully disabling V6? 

The latter is the only piece we didn't have until very recently when @participant1 added it.

> @participant3 made the commit on 30th April but it looks like the 1.22.1 branch didn't pick that change but has more recent commits.

That's correct - there is no IPv6 support in 1.22 AFAIK by design, because it's not stable or (more importantly) covered with automated testing yet. Non-ipv6 fixes have been backported.

> Trying to understand if the platform is literally providing these v4-in-v6 addresses or if we are accidentally mapping them

At least in `istio-cni` we take some pains to always _un_ map them IIRC, so if we have a problem it's likely just V6 itself.
